text: Do you know some of the best pictures of Jupiter were made by people at home?
This is Juno, built from NASA's own 3D model. It reached Jupiter on July fourth, twenty sixteen.
It runs on sunlight. Three arms about nine metres long, covered in more than eighteen thousand solar cells.
That far from the Sun, all of them together make only about five hundred watts.
Jupiter's radiation is brutal. So Juno's electronics sit in a titanium vault, with walls about a centimetre thick.
And its camera, JunoCam, has a special job. NASA posts its raw images online, for anyone.
People around the world download them, and turn them into the pictures of Jupiter you've seen.
Making something together? Orbi Transfer has a board for that.
Everyone posts notes to a bubble board, each person in their own colour. Change one, and everyone sees it marked as edited.
